text.3_Vayera, 20_Siman, 1_Paragraph: And indeed, in truth, this kind of deliverance is more precious even than a deliverance in which there is a human handhold. The prayers in which a person is answered belong to the mystery of direct light (raza d'or yashar); but behold, there are also prayers in which a person is not answered and despairs of them — as in the matter we find in the Talmud (Taanit 24a) concerning several Amoraim who prayed for rain and were not answered, and grew disheartened until they despaired entirely, and only then were answered. This belongs to the mystery of reflected light (raza d'or chozer), and it is higher in rank than a prayer that comes through direct light, since it is from the side of God alone, with no human handhold in it at all. So too was the birth of Isaac regarded in the eyes of Abraham and Sarah: this they believed — that it is nothing beyond God to bring about such a deliverance. Their whole contention, rather, was that this deliverance comes from God's side alone, and that no portion of it should be reckoned to them, as though by their prayer they had effected it. And for this reason God was not displeased with Abraham, since he trusted in God that nothing is too wondrous from God's side. All the displeasure, however, fell upon Sarah. For even though she too believed in God, that from God nothing is withheld — still, in what she said, "and my lord is old" (Gen. 18:12), she pinned a deficiency on Abraham our father: that from him too the expectancy and the hope had run out, just as from her. About this God was exacting — how do you know what depends on another's mind? No person knows what lies in the hidden stores of his fellow. And in this she caused a blemish in "the place that is not known" (atar dela ityada), for it looked as though she pinned the deficiency upon God, God forbid — as though she set a measure and a boundary on God's deliverance, [reasoning] that the whole of the divine governance runs only according to her own grasp: that just as her understanding is limited, so too is the understanding and knowledge of her husband. How do you know the mind of another? This looked as though her faith were not as strong as the faith of Abraham our father, and so God was exacting over this utterance of hers.This is as we find brought in the Tanchuma (Shelach): that God said to the spies — what you said, "and we were in our own eyes as grasshoppers," I waive; but over what you said, "and so we were in their eyes," I am exacting — from where did you know? Perhaps in their eyes you were like angels! For this looks like setting a fixed measure on God's deliverance: as though the whole of God's abundant outflow (shefa) runs only to the limit of their own perception. And likewise they later said, "for he is stronger than us" (Num. 13:31) — as it were (kivyachol), [implying] that the Holy One cannot bring out the divine vessels from there, as is brought in the Talmud (Menachot 53b). And this is the matter [that explains] why, afterward, when God reported Sarah's words to Abraham our father, God altered them for the sake of the ways of peace: for though she said "and my lord is old," God told Abraham that she had said "and I am old" (Gen. 18:13). To understand this — could it ever enter a person's mind that God altered the matter, reporting something that was never said at all? Rather, God set out the [true] sense of her words: that in saying "and my lord is old," her intent was one and the same as had she said "and I am old." That is, she had not concluded that, God forbid, anything is too wondrous for God; rather she was saying that from the creation of the world onward God fixed the nature of the world so that things are created something from something (yesh mi-yesh), and only the creation of the world alone was something from nothing (yesh me-ayin) — but from that point onward it is impossible, within the nature of the world, for something to be created from nothing; only something from something. And as we find with the wife of Obadiah, who came before Elisha the prophet (2 Kings 4:1) and cried out to him, saying, "your servant, my husband, is dead… and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves." And Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said… "a flask of oil." And he said, "Go, borrow yourself empty vessels…" "…and you shall pour into all the vessels…" It is implied from this that had she had nothing at all, the blessing would have had nothing to rest upon.
text.3_Vayera, 40_Siman, 0_Paragraph: And the Lord remembered Sarah, etc. (Genesis 21:1): Behold until this Parashah, it is speaking about the world of chaos; but from this Parashah and onwards, it is speaking about the world of reparation. And for that reason, it is the fourth Parshah, corresponding to the sefirah (emanation) of Eternity (Netzach). For there in the world of chaos, it is written (Genesis 6:6), "And the Lord regretted, etc. and He became saddened to His heart." Whereas this Parashah hints to the sefirah of Eternity - "Moreover, the Netzach of Israel does not deceive or regret, for He is not a man that He should have regrets" (I Samuel 15:29). And for that reason, "And the Lord remembered Sarah, etc.," was also written in this Parashah. That is because the birth of Sarah was also a change in the world. And we read this section on Rosh Hashanah. For there is a change then as well, since every year on Rosh Hashanah, the root of the creation is aroused - as it is found in the holy Zohar (Tetzaveh 184a).
text.4_Chayei Sara, 2_Siman, 3_Paragraph: Rabbi Natan says, "The time of finding (Psalms 32:6) refers to Torah, as it is stated, He who finds Me finds life (Proverbs 8:35)." (Berakhot 8a:11) Torah hints to the specific commandment that is unique to a man in his root source. As every person has a unique commandment that applies to him in his root source, and he has to be more exacting than others about it, in all of its stringencies and its fences. And that way, his root source will be repaired. And it is like the matter that we have found in the Talmud (Shabbat 118b), "In what was your father more careful? In the commandment of tzitzit [fringes]." And the idea in this is that if someone is exacting towards a commandment that does not belong to his root source, and he is more exacting than need be about it due to his confidence that his root source will be repaired — it is about him that it is stated, Do not toil to gain wealth, etc. it grows wings and flies away, like an eagle, heavenward (Proverbs 23:4). And that is that God, may He be blessed, hides the depth of the intention that He has hidden in the act of the commandment. As if there was only the intention in the commandment, then why would God, may He be blessed, have commanded to actually do the commandment. It is implied from this that a person does not have knowledge in this world of the inner hidden words of Torah in the performance of the commandment, And this is like it is found in the Talmud (Sotah 21a), "Rav Yosef said, 'A commandment, at the time when one is engaged in it, protects and saves; at the time when one is not engaged in it, it protects but it does not save.'" And that means that at the time one is not engaged in it, there is nothing of the holiness of the commandment that remains in the body, since the body does not understand its root source. However, a commandment that belongs to a person, especially if he adds to it in its details and its understanding, then God, may He be blessed, enlightens him that he should understand the commandment in the light of the Torah. For all of the essence of the commandments is in the words of the Torah. So he will then have understanding into its intention, and see that the commandment's garment and performance is only in this world. And this is [the meaning of] that which we pray (in the Kedushah of the Order), "May He open our hearts to His Torah," with a vav [making the word possessive, His/his]. This hints to the words of Torah and the commandment that belong especially specifically to each person, according to his root source.
text.4_Chayei Sara, 36_Siman, 0_Paragraph: And these are the generations of Yishmael son of Avraham, etc.: The matter of Yishmael being called the son of Avraham more than the other nations that he fathered afterwards is because at the time of Yishmael's birth, his mother Hagar was still the maidservant of Sarah. As our father Avraham, peace be upon him, was not yet perfected with all types of perfection. That is why there was a little holiness in [Yishmael]. For before a man is perfected, he enters into all sorts of questionable things, since he might gain from them [spiritually]. But with the children that he fathered after Sarah's death when he was perfected with all types of perfection, so that he had no need for any spiritual work at all - given that there was no remaining lack that he needed to perfect - he no longer desired to lower himself and enter into questionable things [from which] he might gain. And because of that, there was no holiness at all or internal power in these children.180As explained above in this Parsha, Section 33.And that is why Yishmaelite converts have a greater status than converts from other nations,181See below, Parshat Toladot, Section 7, staring with the words, "Vezehu."as it is found in the holy Zohar (Parshat Yitro 87a); and he is also more choice than his brothers who were born after the perfection of our father Avraham, as it is found in the holy Zohar.182See the Kometz Mincha, Section 47, by our Master, Rabbi Tzadok HaKohen.But the main holiness of our father Avraham, peace be upon him, was in his son Yitzchak, who was born to him in his hundredth year, at the time that he switched time periods, before he had all of the perfections. But afterwards, he had all the perfections in him; so the main greatness of the [various] levels was then in him. And this is [the meaning] of that which they said in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Lech Lecha 47), "There is an a fortiori argument about the son of the lady: If they (the Yishmaelites) have courtyards and strongholds, all the more so will every righteous person have a world for himself." For God, may He be blessed, shows 'garments' here in this world. For God forbid that he should have perfection in this world; rather Israel perfects that which is lacking. And it is as it is written (Psalms 135:4), "For the Lord (the diminutive two-letter version of God's name is used here) has chosen Yaakov for Himself." And that is because the name of God is only complete (perfected) through Yaakov and Israel, who complete (perfect) the name. And it is, as it were, that God is obligated to lower Himself to save Israel and to destroy all the opponents and accusers from before Israel. And from the son of the maidservant, we learn an a fortiori argument about the son of the lady: If the son of the maidservant, the entire life of whom only came from the statement of Avraham before God, may He be blessed Genesis 17:18), "If only Yishmael might live before you," and God, may He be blessed, answered him (Genesis 17:20), "And as for Yishmael, I have heard you"; all the more so with the son of the lady, about whom God, may He be blessed, said from His angle and from His will (Genesis 17:21), "But I will establish My covenant with Yitzchak," will this last forever and ever. However it is [like this] because God, may He be blessed, does not want to use this in this world, but only in the world that is truly long.
